earlier_scan.source_named: OLAC lists no descriptive resources at all for Nungu/Rindre beyond Ethnologue/LINGUIST List stubs; no wordlist, grammar or phonology located (rogerblench.info also empty for Rindre).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Nunku language of Central Nigeria and its affinities (draft wordlist paper; data collected by Barau Kato 2003).
sources.note: NOT this language: Nunku is a member of the Numana-Nunku-Gwantu-Numbu cluster (Atlas ed. III, entry 343), not Nungu/Rindre. Opened only to rule out the name confusion; it has a §3.3 Tones section and no stress remarks. Not counted as a Nungu source.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. Research on the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 3-44. doi:10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.209
sources.note: Nothing on Nungu phonology. §2.4 Ninzic (p. 24): 'Descriptive materials on Ninzic are sparse'; specific-language materials named are Hoffmann 1976, Hörner 1980 (Ninzam), Price 1989 (Mada), Ninzo LPC 1999, Wilson 2003 (Kuche), Blench & Kato in progress (Mada) — none for Nungu. Nungu figures only in the classification table (Table 3) and in the note that Shimizu 1975a used it lexicostatistically. No 'stress'/'accent' anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Nigeria Bible Translation Trust (NBTT), Rindre Project. 2020. Rindre [rin] scripture drafts: Matthew (rin_mat_text_reg), John (rin_jhn_text_reg), 1 Corinthians (rin_1co_text_reg), Galatians (rin_gal_text_reg), 2 Timothy (rin_2ti_text_reg). translationStudio-desktop repositories, user 'nbtt', Wycliffe Associates Content Service, created 2020-09-16.
sources.note: Primary text only, no linguistic front matter. Observation (not a statement by the source): the practical orthography used throughout Matthew 5 is plain ASCII Latin with digraphs (gh, kp, ny, sh, ng) and carries no diacritics whatsoever, i.e. tone is not marked in the NBTT Rindre orthography; e.g. Mt 5:3 'Dubo usu ti mba nima su na ugru ni uhu risi, shakpa kpare su ti tama.' An NBTT orthography statement for Rindre presumably exists offline (NBTT, Jos) and is the document to request.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 1), 107-172. Berlin: Language Science Press. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1314325
sources.note: Nothing on Nungu prosody; the chapter explicitly records that information on Nungu nominal morphology is inadequate ('Nungu | Information inadequate', Table 4), confirming that as of 2018 Blench held no analysed Rindre data beyond wordlists. Tone is discussed only for other Ninzic languages (e.g. 'Ningye-Ninka: Alternating prefixes lost, tone plurals'; Ayu 'c. tone-change'). The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the chapter.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th edition. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Nungu' [rin] (open the Internet Archive capture of ethnologue.com/language/rin, 2016).

sources.note: Silent. The 2016 entry consists only of Alternate Names, Population (50,000, 1999), Location (Nasarawa: Wamba, Akwanga, Nasarawa-Eggon LGAs; Kaduna: Sanga, Jema'a, Kaura; Plateau: Riyom, Bokkos), Language Status 6a (Vigorous), Classification (Niger-Congo.. Plateau, Western, Southwestern, A), Dialects (Rindre, Gudi) and Language Resources (OLAC link); there is no 'Typology' field (where Ethnologue would note tone), and no 'Language Development', 'Writing' or 'Other Comments' field - so as of 2016 Ethnologue knew of no literacy material, orthography statement or survey report for Rindre. sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed. (version 03 Dec 2012). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 386 'Rindre'.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 386 Rindre: names Rendre, Rindiri, Lindiri; Wamba, Nungu; Nasarawa State, Akwanga LGA; 10,000 (1972 Welmers), 25,000 (SIL); Benue-Congo: Plateau: Ninzic; dialects Rindre, Gudi; second language Hausa; 'Source(s) Kato (2008)'. No linguistic description, no literacy materials listed.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. (page dated 2011/2015). Ninzic languages: wordlists & papers. Web page, rogerblench.info (the Internet Archive 2025-05-28).
sources.note: Index page only. Lists wordlists for Anib, Ayu, Bu, Ce, Mada, Ningye, Ninka, Ninkyop, Ninzo, Numana, Nunku — no Rindre/Nungu item. (The 'Nunku' wordlist is a different language, see next row.) Confirms the earlier scan note that Blench's site has nothing for Rindre.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2008. Prospecting proto-Plateau. Ms. (rogerblench.info, the Internet Archive 2025-05-28).
sources.note: Nothing. Nungu appears only as a row in classification tables and in two comparative lexical sets (mekru, ubye); no phonological description; 'stress'/'accent' absent.

sources.citation: Olson, Kenneth S. & John Hajek. 2004. A crosslinguistic lexicon of the labial flap. Linguistic Discovery 2(2). Hanover, NH: Dartmouth College Library. doi:10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.262. Section 3.2 Platoid, 3.2.1 'Nungu [RIN, p1] (Nigeria)'; its source is Peust, Carsten. 1997. Sum: Bilabial trill. LINGUIST List 8.45 (17 Jan 1997), relaying Mary Ward (maryward@mail.utexas.edu).
sources.note: Nothing on tone or stress. The only Nungu content is segmental and secondhand: sec. 3.2.1 quotes the 1997 LINGUIST posting that, according to Mary Ward, Rindre/Nungu/Wamba 'possesses a labiodental flap', and adds 'No articulatory description or data are given.' The whole article (69k chars of text) was searched: Nungu/Rindre/Wamba occur only in this entry. Value: it documents that an American linguist (Mary Ward, UT Austin address in 1997) had first-hand Rindre data in the 1990s that were never published - a person-level retrieval lead, and the only published phonological remark of any kind o…

sources.citation: Gerhardt, Ludwig. 1983. The classification of Eggon: Plateau or Benue group? Journal of West African Languages 13(1): 37-50.
sources.note: Nothing on Rindre/Nungu prosody. The phonological discussion (CCV root shapes, metathesis, sound correspondences) concerns Eggon dialects only; Rindre contributes five untoned lexical forms (drink 'waa', path 'u-shi', meat 'u-be', fire '[u-la]', four '-ne') in a comparative table. Wordlist-level data only for this languoid; no tone marks on the Rindre row and no remark on tone or stress for any Plateau 5 language other than Eggon.

sources.citation: ComparaLex records 'Nungu 1 (Nungu)' (w1=256, 109 words, untoned) and 'Nungu 2 (Nungu)' (w1=257, 43 words, tone-marked) [rin]: digitisation of the Nungu (Lindiri) lists in Williamson, Kay & Kiyoshi Shimizu (eds.) 1968 / Williamson (ed.) 1973, Benue-Congo Comparative Wordlist, vols. I-II. Ibadan: West African Linguistic Society; data submitted to ComparaLex by Roger Blench; copyright Kay Williamson.
sources.note: No prose statement (bare wordlist). The Nungu 2 transcriptions carry three tone diacritics — acute, grave and vertical line (mid), e.g. 003 ARMPIT lalá, 005 ASHES ò-kro, 012 BUFFALO mɛ-rɛ́, 023 CRAB la̍-krɔ̀, 043 FOWL me-nà, 090 STONE kí-kɛ̀, 102 WOMAN o-ŋá, 104 TWO o-hà, 108 SIX a̍ndra̍ — i.e. the BCCW fieldworker transcribed Nungu with (at least) three contrastive pitch levels, which is first-hand evidence that the language is tonal, but it is data, not a statement, and says nothing about stress. Nungu 1 (109 items) is untoned.

sources.citation: Mathews, H. F. 1917. Notes on the Nungu tribe, Nassawara Province, Northern Nigeria, and the neighboring tribes which use the duodecimal system of numeration. Harvard African Studies 1: 83-93.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic notes plus a comparative table of numerals 1-12+ for Nungu, South Mada, Mama and Ninzam (pp. 92-93); the author says he could not collect large vocabularies; no remarks on accent, tone or pronunciation of Nungu.

sources.note: Nothing. Wikipedia is a stub citing Ethnologue (dialects Rinde/Rindre and Gudi, ~30,000 speakers 1999); Wikitongues lists no resources; Joshua Project: Bible translation 'started', Global Recordings audio only. sources.citation: Kato, Barau. 2008. Rindre wordlist / field notes (unpublished; sole source named for the Rindre entry in Blench, Atlas of Nigerian Languages ed. III, entry 386).

sources.note: Only known primary field data on Rindre; Blench/Kato wordlist papers normally carry a short phonology with a Tones section, so this is the one item likely to say whether the language is tonal and whether stress plays any role.

sources.note: The main descriptive work on Plateau (Greenberg's groups 2 and 4) noun-class languages; whether it contains any Nungu material is unverified (Nungu was Plateau 5 in the older classification, so probably not), but it is the only substantial descriptive monograph on the neighbouring Ninzic languages.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1975. A lexicostatistical study of Plateau languages and Jukun. Anthropological Linguistics 17(9): 413-418.

sources.note: Used Nungu data; lexicostatistics only, so low chance of a stress remark, but it is one of the few published works with Nungu forms.

sources.citation: [Student author not shown on the reseller pages]. n.d. [c. 2011]. Negation in Nungu Language. B.A. long essay, 65 pp., chapters 1-5 (Government-and-Binding framework; cites Yusuf 1997, Lamidi 2000, Williamson 1982, Crozier & Blench 1976). Institution not printed in the preview; the framework, house style and the sibling titles listed with it (Negation in Yeskwa/Kuturmi, Aspects of Adim/Atsam phonology, Kaningkon verb phrase, etc.) identify it as one of the University of Ilorin Department of Linguistics & Nigerian Languages long essays of the 2011 series. Distributed as 'project material' by eduprojecttopics.com and samphina.com.ng (chapter one previewed openly; full text on payment).
